newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria replaces hardline gendarmerie chief.
newsitem.headline: Algeria replaces hardline gendarmerie chief.

text.p: Algerian President Liamine Zeroual on Monday removed hardline anti-Islamist Major-General Benabbes Ghezaiel from his post as commander of the crack paramilitary gendarmerie forces.
Ghezaiel was replaced by Zeroual's top defence adviser Tayeb Derradji, an army major-general.
An official statement, reported by the Algerian news agency APS, said Ghezaiel was "called to take up other duties", a term widely used for officials moved to the sidelines.
Ghezaiel played an instrumental role in Algeria's struggle against radical Moslem fundamentalists who have been fighting the authorities for nearly six years.
The highly politicised and well disciplined gendarmerie forces have been at the forefront of the battle to check the guerrillas.
Ghezaiel's removal was the latest change in the army hierarchy since the appointment of Zeroual as defence minister in July 1993.

President Zeroual, who keeps the post of defence minister and army commander-in-chief, was appointed head of state in January 1994 and four months later picked the then general Tayeb Derradji as his adviser.
Zeroual was returned to power late in 1995 when he overwhelmed his three contenders in the country's first plural presidential poll.
In June 1996, he appointed general Saheb Madjid as new chief for the fourth military region which controls the country's main oil and gas producing areas in the south.
Madjid replaced major-general Madjid Saidi Fodhil who had been killed in a car accident earlier that month.
Zeroual, the same month, also appointed general Kamel Abderrahmane as army chief in charge of the vital Oran western region where Algeria's oil and gas export outlets are based.
